Where the repo carries no docs/agents/ overlay at all (e.g. a skill-source repo), substitute the closest repo doctrine you can find (README, CONTRIBUTING, top-level docs) and record the substitution — do not treat those paths as guaranteed to exist. Before you open any source file, resolve and read the map input: run py /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-commander/scripts/map_orient.py orient --root /home/tommy/projects/constellation-skills-wt/c3-lifecycle --work-id epic-559/c3-lifecycle. On RESOLVED, read the entrypoint it names and the packets, overlays and decision anchors it routes you to for the area the ask touches, and treat every later source read as confirming a frame the map already gave you rather than building one out of code. On DEGRADED, re-run the same command with --substitute PATH (what you read instead of a map — it is hash-pinned into the receipt) --unmapped TEXT (what stayed unmapped) --escalation TEXT (what you are escalating, and to whom), and get that on the record before any source read: degraded is a declared reading, never a licence to start from code. The tool probes a fixed fallback order — README.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, a docs/ index — and labels a substitute it found there as verified by the filesystem rather than merely asserted by you. The anchor of this instruction is the point: 'before you open any source file' is an act you cannot postpone, whereas a map-first imperative anchored to a late artifact (the gate plan, which is authored at the END of a long run) is satisfied by a run that crawls source for fifty calls, reads the map afterwards, and has complied exactly — that is measured behaviour, not a hypothetical. plan.title: Author the gate plan
plan.imperative: Map-first: BEFORE authoring execute.json, produce a mission frame from the map input the context step resolved, using templates/MISSION_FRAME.template.md (intent; affected capabilities; relevant examples/events; structural anchors; governing constraints/assumptions; decision anchors and decision pressure; claims/evidence surfaces; map confidence/staleness/disputes; out of scope). Write it to .agent-work/epic-559/c3-lifecycle/MISSION_FRAME.md — that exact path is what the c6 gate reads, so a frame parked anywhere else reads as no frame at all. For a trivial local/mechanical change where the map adds nothing, shrink or skip the frame and say so in its intent; c6 is waivable, so take that escape as a RECORDED waiver (<engine> waive plan --cond c6 --authority human --reason '...') rather than as a silent skip. The c6 gate runs map_orient.py verify-frame over that file: every anchor id the frame cites must exist in the map inventory the context step resolved, or — when context came back DEGRADED — must be one of the substitutes the receipt hash-pinned there, so the frame is compared against a committed prior declaration instead of a same-breath assertion. Know what that check is and is not, and do not overclaim it: it is a regression floor so map-IGNORING cannot silently return, not the fix for map-LATENESS. Measured against this epic's baseline five runs it has sensitivity 0/4 and specificity 0/1, and it inherits the late-anchor defect it was built next to, because anchors-in-a-late-frame is compliance without sequence. The load-bearing map-first anchor is at the context step ('before you open any source file'), which is why verify-orientation is gated there and verify-frame is gated only here. Do NOT 'fix' that asymmetry by also running verify-frame at context: no frame exists at context — the step runs before understand and plan — and the only way to make it pass there is to let an ABSENT frame pass, which is exactly the refusal the whole check is built on. If verify-frame ever has to be context-safe, give it a step-scoped mode; never a vacuous pass. For any low-confidence/stale/disputed map area the run depends on, alter the plan accordingly: add a scout/verification gate or surface it to the human as a decision — never author gates that silently trust an unverified map. Surface durable-structure choices as decision candidates per the skill's Decision candidates section rather than choosing alone. Then author the gate plan into execute.json: each gate the smallest reasonable bite, with close criteria, required evidence, and an anchors block cut from the frame. Before the plan-approved checkpoint run plan-alternatives (parallel gate-plan candidates under distinct constraints, via the references/design-it-twice-brief.md contract) and a cold plan critic (reads the candidate plan + mission frame only, no authoring context); both bias-to-yes — any skip is surfaced as a named untaken road — and the panel-vs-single choice is surfaced to the human at plan approval. execute.context_headroom_note: #467. Absolute-token context reserve for THIS gate only: the engine subtracts it from both the soft and hard caps before dividing by the model's window, so `execute` may not be BEGUN with less than this much room left below the hard cap. It makes the imperative's existing prose instruction ('ensure context headroom before entering') enforceable, and it can only ever tighten -- no gate can raise a threshold. WHY 30000, and it is a GUESS, revisable in place: `execute` is the run's longest gate and the one that cannot be abandoned halfway, because it drives every crew gate and each crew dispatch costs tens of thousands of tokens. The only observation available was a commander sitting at ~127K fill after a cold resume plus one full three-task gate -- which bounds one gate's marginal cost in the tens of thousands but cannot separate it from the resume baseline. 30K is a round number at the low end of that range: on claude-opus-5 (1M window, 80K soft / 150K hard) it moves execute's begin-work line from 15% to 12% and its advisory from 8% to 5%, while every other gate keeps the shipped default. The named settle experiment (read fill_fraction across completed commander runs at the moment execute was started) is NOT runnable from existing artifacts -- gauge.json keeps only the latest reading and the per-gate context manifests record no fill -- so a later run may revise this number here, in this one place, without re-deriving anything.

None of the old is-.agent-work-gitignored reasoning applies to it. Push the branch to remote. When you open a PR on Windows, write the body to a temp file and use gh pr create -F <file> — a bash heredoc and a PowerShell @'...'@ here-string both fail for gh pr create --body (here-strings work for git commit -m, not PR bodies). Release the engine session lease only as your VERY LAST action, AFTER the archive postconditions pass and you have run the engine's final advance on archive (the advance that marks the spine done): by default call the spine_lease MCP tool with action=release (this is your own spine; the door needs no session id argument). CLI fallback: <engine> release --session-id commander-epic-559/c3-lifecycle. Release must come after that closing advance, never before it — the lease must cover every journaled action, so the release is the final journal entry; releasing earlier leaves archive's own closeout entries (attest/waive/advance) after the lease release and fails the terminal provenance check.

the work is REACHABLE: this branch has a pull request that is OPEN or MERGED. A merged PR is reachable work; a closed-unmerged one is not, and neither is no PR at all. A terminal spine and a pushed branch describe the run, not the ref -- CI never runs on an unopened branch, and every commander that reached a terminal spine without opening one had to be chased for it. Open the PR even if the work is unfinished; declare FINAL or PENDING in its title and hand the merge up. Two properties of the check text are load-bearing. triage_candidates.statement: The door binds ONE spine per process, but a Commander drives TWO checklists — its spine and its gate plan. _identity_violation refuses any argv resolving --file off the bound spine, so GATE_PLAN.json cannot be driven through this door at all. The only shipped way to drive a second checklist is a second, differently-bound server hand-registered in the user-level ~/.claude.json — verified: that is exactly what the Admiral's own `spine-epic` entry is, bound to .agent-work/epic-418-followon/spine.json. So the corpus's answer to "drive a second checklist" is a manual config edit that cannot even take effect mid-session, which is the same unautomated class as the hand-typed `git worktree add` this epic exists to remove. This does NOT invalidate the deliverable (a crew binds a generated spine through run_crew.py --spine, which works), but it does mean this Commander executes its own gate plan as a frozen document, running every close-criterion command itself, rather than through the engine. Recorded rather than routed around.

why_trail.why: Work area was scaffolded and this spine instantiated and bound by the Admiral at launch (LAUNCH_ORDER "Pre-rulings": init is done — attest and move). Isolation precondition verified in-worktree; lease claimed by this session.

Project posture read: workflow mechanisms are a "strengthened durable system" — targeted automated tests plus the broader suite, and pushes/merges to main need explicit human approval (the launch order already forbids them). Two facts change how I will plan: (1) docs/agents/engine-config.json, which this spine's own config_ref names, does not exist — the engine is running on defaults; (2) there is no Cartographer packet map at all, so the mission frame will be built from the code map, README, and the C2 DESIGN_NOTE contract rather than from map anchors, and that degradation is on the record with hash-pinned substitutes.

Reconciled the launch order against the code before planning, and one of its six baseline claims changed the design. The order names the door's import-time SPINE_FILE KeyError as the chicken-and-egg; measured, .mcp.json supplies a shell default so the server always starts. The real obstacle is two other properties: _identity_violation refuses any argv resolving --file away from the bound spine, and test_mcp_identity's choke-point pin AST-restricts every return in call_tool to as_result(run_engine(...)) or _tool_error(...). So an open tool is not an engine verb and must not pretend to be one. Second measurement that settles the Admiral's question 2: the engine round-trips an unknown top-level spine key intact through claim/start/attest/advance, and validate_spine has no unknown-key fault, so the worktree record can live INSIDE the spine with zero engine change. Third: crew-runs.json records parent and model per entry, which makes the declared dispatch checkable data rather than prose to retype. Baselines reproduced exactly on 293b7721: 2824 passed / 3 skipped / 1121 subtests, and 23 sweep fault lines.
